gates.description: Four golden signals must be exported: latency, traffic, errors, saturation
Structured JSON logging must be configured with trace_id and span_id
Distributed tracing must be configured with OpenTelemetry or equivalent
Every alert must link to a dashboard and runbook
Log and metric retention policies must be defined (hot/warm/cold)
PII and sensitive data must not be logged

anti_patterns.description: Service built first, instrumentation added months later when debugging becomes impossible
Hundreds of dashboards, most outdated, nobody knows which one to use
Storing every log line at DEBUG level forever — log storage costs exceed compute costs
A dashboard shows a spike but there's no way to investigate — metrics without traces, traces without logs
The observability pipeline itself has no monitoring — when it fails, engineers don't know their monitoring is broken

escalation_triggers: Observability pipeline failure causing loss of production visibility
Instrumentation gap in a critical service discovered during an incident
Observability costs growing significantly faster than the services they monitor
Data retention policies conflict with compliance requirements
Vendor lock-in concerns with current observability backend
Significant number of services deployed without basic observability

input_requirements.description: Spec.md with service definitions and SLO requirements

output_certifications: Four golden signals exported for all services (latency, traffic, errors, saturation)
Structured JSON logging configured with trace_id context propagation
Distributed tracing pipeline configured (OpenTelemetry SDK integrated)
All alerts link to relevant dashboards and runbooks
No PII or sensitive data in logs or traces
